findings.failure_path: The ancestry check captures the outer base_ref instead of the current recursive walk's base. Construct O→T on the target, where T changes only an unrelated file. A feature forks at O, commits owner work W, automatically merges T as S, then appends the valid row at L. Against T, the branch passes: S is a base sync and W plus L share a round. Merge L into T and evaluate the integration against O: expansion starts the recursive walk at T, but S is now expanded because T is not an ancestor of outer base O or W. The resulting [T,W] span contains owner work without its row and reports impact_chain_gate_missing. A valid branch therefore becomes red on promotion.
findings.smallest_fix: Pass the current walk's from into expandable_merge and also exclude second parents ancestral to that local base. Add this nested target-sync fixture with branch and promotion verdict assertions.

findings.failure_path: The plain git merge-base invocation never checks its exit status. If ancestry checks and merge-tree succeed but this invocation exits 128 without stdout, fork becomes empty and expansion silently falls back to the collapsed boundary. For the row-before-work fixture, that changes the required refusal into acceptance—the same leniency round scoping 8 removes.
findings.smallest_fix: Capture and validate this invocation's exit status immediately. Abort with impact_chain_git_failed on unexpected failures, and add a fault-injection test showing that a failing fork lookup cannot produce a passing collapsed verdict.

findings.failure_path: The new trust boundary enumerates evidence from the landing checkout, but the bounded packet omits scan, validator_accepts, candidate_scope, and the closeout-writing fixture implementation. Its new tests cover only matching versus different digests. Consequently, the required check cannot establish whether dirty or untracked evidence is excluded, rejected or forged closeouts remain rejected, and later evidence cannot alter packet exclusions. The claimed retrospective closeout is also absent from the supplied diff.
findings.smallest_fix: Supply the relevant enumeration, validation, and scope implementations plus landing-tree negative fixtures for uncommitted and rejected evidence, packet/base/exclude invariance, and the retrospective closeout needed to verify containment.

concern_results.conclusion: Static counterexamples show that nested sync merges can split a previously valid round, and an unchecked merge-base failure can restore the lenient collapsed verdict.

Digest comparison and validator invocation remain visible, but the packet cannot establish committed-only evidence enumeration or rejection of forged, unvalidated, and uncommitted landing-tree evidence.

challenge_focus: Adversarial: (1) any way a merge that git did not fully reproduce, or whose second parent is a sync of the base or of the line, gets expanded or gets a lenient span — including git failures whose exit status is swallowed; (2) any way expansion lets owner work sit in no round or lets a row cover work outside its round, versus the branch-head view CI evaluates; (3) any way reading chain evidence from the landing tree accepts a ledger that the round-checkout rule would have refused (forged, other digest, unvalidated, uncommitted), or changes the round packet, base or excludes.
